name: Learn basic negotiation techniques
blurb: Preparation, anchoring, silence and knowing your walkaway. A few hours of study measurably changes salary, rent and contract outcomes for the rest of your life.
gear: A book or course on principled negotiation
A real negotiation to practise on
steps: Prepare properly: know your target, your walkaway point, and your best alternative if no deal happens. That alternative is your real leverage.
Research the other side’s interests, not just their position — what they actually need may be cheap for you to give.
Learn anchoring: the first credible number shapes the range. Make it justified rather than arbitrary.
Learn to use silence after an offer. Most people negotiate against themselves to fill it.
Trade rather than concede: never give something without getting something.
Practise on small things — a market stall, a service contract — before anything that matters.
tips: Never accept the first offer, and never make an offer you cannot justify.
A negotiation you would rather lose than damage the relationship is a different game. Decide which one you are in.
The willingness to walk away is worth more than any tactic.
proof: You negotiate a real outcome — pay, rent, a contract — measurably better than the opening offer.
